skills.trigger: When evaluating a patient with dysphonia and a suspected tracheal or mediastinal malignancy to identify the radiographic correlate of nerve involvement.
steps: Inspect the axial CT image at the level of the thoracic inlet or upper mediastinum to assess the paratracheal regions and hila.
Identify any soft tissue mass or lymphadenopathy specifically in the left paratracheal or left hilar region adjacent to the trachea.

Correlate left-sided paratracheal/hilar pathology with dysphonia by recognizing the anatomical course of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve as it loops under the aortic arch near this location, distinguishing it from right-sided or peripheral lung findings which are less likely to cause this specific symptom via nerve compression.
